items.excerpt: Strong gaming chops in a slim and lightweight chassis.
items.content_text: Walmart's GeForce Week Sale is ending soon, but there's still time to pick up a great deal on a powerful gaming laptop. For a limited time, Walmart has the Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop for just $1,449.00 with free shipping. In addition to the powerful GPU, the A16 Pro comes preinstalled with 32GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD, which means you don't need to go out and pay an exorbitant amount of money to add more. Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop for $1,449 The Gigabyte A16 Pro laptop measures 0.77" at its thinnest point and weighs just 5 pounds, which is light for a 16" gaming laptop. It's equipped with a 16" 2560x1600 165Hz IPS display, Intel Core 7 240H CPU, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 12GB GPU with 115W TGP, 32GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. The Intel Core 7 240H is a 10-core CPU with a max turbo frequency of 5.2GHz. This is a solid, efficient processor for gaming. The RAM is not user upgradeable so it's good that the system already includes 32GB pre-installed. The SSD, on the other hand, is user-upgradeable. Compared to Nvidia's previous generation RTX 4000 mobile GPUs, it's comparable in performance to the RTX 4080 and pulls ahead of it in games that support DLSS 4.5 and multi-frame generation. The A16 Pro's 5070 Ti GPU is throttled down to 115W TGP instead of the usual 140W max in order to cut down on heat, but it's powerful enough to run most games smoothly on the display's 1600p resolution from classic favs like League of Legends, Roblox, or Fortnite to new releases like Onimusha: Way of the Sword . items.title: Arc Raiders Is Testing a PvE Mode Very Soon
items.excerpt: Embark Studios has announced that it will be testing a PvE mode for Arc Raiders next month.
items.content_text: Embark Studios has announced that it will be testing a PvE mode for Arc Raiders next month. From October 13 to October 20, Arc Raiders will have a PvE toggle, allowing you to seamlessly switch between lobbies where you can fight other players and lobbies where players can't do damage to you. The aim is to give players more choice and test the ability to let players completely disengage from PvP gameplay. As a result, loot in PvE will be lower-valued because the mode has lower stakes. Additionally, ARCs will target downed players to create some form of tension, but if players stay still, they will be ignored by AI foes. Embark will be monitoring the player economy and matchmaking times during this period. The team has noted that "it's possible that this will not work," meaning PvE may not actually make its way into the game permanently. This is a test to see how well they can make it'll operate, rather than some kind of stress test. "It’s important to mention that this is not a risk-free test," said the studio . "The first, unlaunched iteration of ARC Raiders was conceived as a PvE game, and we have been hesitant to return to that concept. There is a risk that introducing a PvE matchmaking toggle could reduce some of the tension that the game was built around. At the same time, we have to respect that some players want to enjoy the game in their own way, and we can’t ignore what the data is telling us. "As creators, we design a game with an intention for how we think it should be played; but after launch, it becomes the players’ game. This is one of the unique and wonderful things about making games; we build something with a specific vision, and then we get to see players finding their own ways to enjoy it." The reason for the test is that Embark Studios' data demonstrated that a sizable amount of players ignored or tried to avoid combat against other players. They were more interested in a co-op, social experience rather than one where they had to fight real humans. You can view some of the data directly from Embark below. 37% Friendly co-op players (this player group has grown consistently since launch). 27% Mixed players. 34% Pure PvP players (this player group has remained stable since launch). Over 70% of Friendly players and even 40% of PvP players express a desire for fewer hostile encounters and 51% of the surveyed player base has expressed an interest in a dedicated PvE option. It'll be interesting to see what comes of this test and it's refreshing to see a studio experimenting with something so publicly, even if it doesn't result in any permanent changes. Either way, the community will have to show whether it wants Arc Raiders to have PvE or not and provide actionable feedback to make it feasible.
items.title_en: Arc Raiders Is Testing a PvE Mode Very Soon

items.title: Ubisoft Almost Made a Zelda Game With Ganondorf as the Protagonist
items.excerpt: Ubisoft Milan reportedly pitched a Zelda game to Nintendo that would have taken place in a new universe with a totally different protagonist, but the plan fell through, leading to one of the biggest what-ifs in gaming history.
items.content_text: Ubisoft Milan reportedly pitched a Zelda game to Nintendo that would have taken place in a new universe with a totally different protagonist, but the plan fell through, leading to one of the biggest what-ifs in gaming history. Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson says the project was internally titled Goliath, so as to appropriately echo the size and scale of what Ubisoft Milan hoped to achieve with the game. It was an ambitious plan, and one that former Ubisoft developer Gian Marco Zanna described as a “new big bang in the video game universe.” This description, while dramatic, is accurate; Ubisoft Milan’s Zelda game would have been drastically different from anything we’ve seen from the series thus far. Rather than following Link’s adventures in the wilds of Hyrule, it would have been a spin-off title in the broader Zelda universe featuring a brand-new, “never-before-seen character.” However, during its early concept phase, Nintendo reportedly asked that this protagonist be changed to the franchise’s ultimate big bad: Ganondorf. This would have been the first time Ganondorf was the central, playable character in a Zelda game, and on paper, it sounds like a fantastic idea… but unfortunately, it didn’t end up coming to fruition. Sources told Henderson that Ubisoft Milan was given a deadline of late 2023 to come up with a prototype for this Ganondorf game, but Nintendo reportedly rejected their proposal when the time came, for reasons that have not been made clear. Ubisoft Milan was behind the highly-lauded Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope, which IGN scored a sparkling nine out of 10 . The studio reportedly began ideation for Goliath shortly after its release, clearly riding the high of its successful launch. It’s almost painful to imagine the game we could’ve had; perhaps it was a Ganon origin story? Given that it was a spin-off and not a sequel or prequel, it’s unclear what, exactly, Ganon would be doing in this game. And what about Ubisoft Milan’s first intended protagonist for the project? We have so many questions, and it’s likely that none of them will ever get answered. Ubisoft did not respond to Henderson’s requests for comment, but he did note that it had internally acknowledged a journalist requesting information about Goliath beforehand. Among the oodles of canceled, top-secret games over the years, this one definitely makes us go down the ‘what if’ rabbit hole. It’s almost as tantalizing as the canceled Disney Smash Bros.-style game , which former concept artist Ken Christiansen shared artwork for on his personal online portfolio, showing characters like Captain Hook, the Sheriff of Nottingham, the Queen of Hearts, John Silver, and others facing off in 2v2 battles.
items.title_en: Ubisoft Almost Made a Zelda Game With Ganondorf as the Protagonist

items.title: Target Confirms Jack Skellington's Real-Life Height in a New Halloween Sale Listing
items.content_text: How tall is Jack Skellington? Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas is an animated movie, so there hasn't been any sort of official confirmation of the iconic skeleton's measurements. Thankfully, Target is selling a Jack Skellington decoration in its larger Halloween sale that gives us the most accurate estimate we've seen so far. According to the listing, Skellington stands at 6'6" tall. This is an officially licensed Disney product and clearly states this version of the skeleton is "life-size", so it's the closest thing to canon we'll likely ever get. Note : Target's Halloween decoration sale is online-only and will end on September 26. Jack Skellington's true height has been a subject of debate since the movie came out. There's an entire Reddit thread that goes into his potential proportions as well as his apparent fire-resistance. While that thread theorizes that he's actually 11 feet tall, 6'6" seems a lot more reasonable. He towers over the mayor of Halloween Town, sure, but he's only about a head taller than Sally. As for the actual decoration, it's a fully-realized Jack Skellington figure that is able to stand on its own. He's dressed up in his pinstripe suit and can sing "Jack's Lament" while moving his arm and hand around. It's normally priced at $329.99, but Target is offering a 20% off sale that drops the price down pretty significantly. Also, the LEGO Nightmare Before Christmas Set Is Retiring Speaking of The Nightmare Before Christmas, it's worth calling out that the iconic LEGO set for the movie is officially "retiring soon." LEGO recently added the set to its list of sets that are going to be disappearing, most likely at the end of 2026. We had the pleasure of building this set ourselves when it first came out and absolutely loved its dedication to the film.

items.title: This Cozy Dressmaking Game is Taking Over Steam's Top Sellers List
items.excerpt: Dressmaker, an indie game where you run a boutique and design dresses, is taking over Steam, becoming one of the platform’s Top 10 best-selling games mere days after its release.
items.content_text: Dressmaker, an indie game where you run a boutique and design dresses, is taking over Steam, becoming one of the platform’s Top 10 best-selling games mere days after its release. If you’re on gaming Twitter, you’ve likely come across clips from a game where players are carefully stitching together fabric to make ornate gowns. That’s no coincidence; Dressmaker, the game in question, is having a moment right now, and Steam’s best sellers list proves it. At the time of writing this article on September 24, Dressmaker has reached tenth place on Steam’s Top Sellers list . It’s also earned an Overwhelmingly Positive rating, with 96% of 2,177 user reviews being positive. Dressmaker has beaten out massive titles like Diablo IV and even had the upper hand over Marvel Rivals for a moment. Its popularity is sparking a wave of interest in the game, as well as starting an interesting conversion on social media regarding smaller games that are made to suit a niche audience versus big-budget, AAA titles designed to appeal to as many players as possible. One Twitter/X user described it best : “Take game marketed towards women and creatives / optimise it so it can run on most shitty laptops and PCs that have been sold in the last 10 years / fill it with whimsy and genuine respect for the craft it’s emulating / make a billion dollars.’ “Hey look, a niche game appealing directly to a target audience that loves it. Amazing,” another wrote , comparing the game to AAA titles that “look so generic I can’t tell them apart.” “We need more of this! Make more games targeting specific audiences instead of bastardizing successful IPs to fit ‘everybody,’” another said . Dressmaker was developed by Cozy Lives and published by Free Lives, an independent game studio based in Cape Town, South Africa that’s behind games like Genital Jousting and Terra Nil. In Dressmaker, players own and operate their very own dress boutique, where they design and sew dresses for customers in a fictional town. It’s not just a dress-up game, though; you can also “sabotage” your clientele if you want to make the stakes a little higher. This is the latest indie game to go viral on social media following Stray Dog: nobody cares , a Soulslike game where you play as a stray dog on a quest to rescue its master using an old, rusty sword it wields in its jaws.

items.title: Warcraft 3 Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom Review
items.excerpt: A surprise single-player campaign that maintains the feel of classic Warcraft 3 while mixing in some new ideas.
items.content_text: I was a bit stunned to hear there's a new single-player story campaign for Warcraft 3 in 2026 – 23 years after its last expansion, The Frozen Throne . And after the uneven Warcraft 3 Reforged, I was even more surprised at how much I ended up enjoying Forsaken Kingdom and its accompanying changes. It's honestly great to be back looking down at Azeroth's moody champions and impressive cities from a raven's eye view considering Blizzard hasn't given single-player RTS fans anything new to chew on since 2016's Starcraft II: Nova Covert Ops. This expansion maintains the feel of classic Warcraft 3 while mixing in some new ideas, and while it doesn’t hit the highs of Reign of Chaos or The Frozen Throne, that's something I might never run out of appetite for. This review will cover three main additions to Reforged that all arrived together: the Forsaken Kingdom single-player campaign expansion itself, the Forsaken Paladin multiplayer hero, and the "Definitive Edition" graphics update that was made to address criticisms of 2020's redone art style. Let's start with the campaign. Forsaken Kingdom kicks off with the four-mission Last Days of Lordaeron prologue campaign, which is quite juicy and ambitious on its own. It picks up on the day Arthas returned from Northrend to kill his father, perhaps one of the most pivotal moments in all of Warcraft lore, and follows the new hero, guard lieutenant Garek Bandarion, as he fights his way through a besieged Andorhal and a devastated Strathholme in a doomed attempt to save his homeland from the Scourge. This chapter culminates with a confrontation against none other than Baron Rivendare, and contains numerous clever little references to both Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft. I enjoyed the design of these missions for the most part, as they take after the classic RTS formula of Warcraft 3. The Siege of Andorhal, especially, puts a little bit of a MOBA-inspired twist on the typical Warcraft 3 routine by having you capture towers that spawn waves of CPU-controlled friendly soldiers at regular intervals to help you push across the map. Another segment of the same mission required me to hold specific objectives to be able to recruit certain kinds of units, rather than simply needing their associated structure in my base. Stratholme, post-purge at this point, is built like a winding dungeon crawl. Stratholme, post-purge at this point, is built like a winding dungeon crawl that requires you to coordinate one group led by Garek and a second led by the elven priest Ilastar Songbreeze – 500 bonus points if you recognize that deep cut, because I definitely had to look up who the heck he was and I practically eat, sleep, and breathe Warcraft. They remain separated for the first half of the mission, which created some interesting opportunities to use one group to complete an objective that helped the other progress. They then unite at the end for the final, dramatic push, which ties the whole scenario together nicely. In an extremely heavily-telegraphed twist, Garek doesn't fare well in his confrontation with Rivendare, and ends up raised as one of the free-willed Forsaken in the main campaign. Taking his orders directly from Sylvanas and accompanied by her lieutenant, the Dark Ranger Anya, this free-roaming, quest-driven adventure revolves around establishing the Forsaken in the Undercity beneath the capital ruins. If you played the Founding of Durotar epilogue campaign in the original, you kind of know what to expect. What I said about Warcraft 3: Reforged Warcraft 3 is still probably my favorite Warcraft game of all time, and one of my favorite fantasy stories in any video game. The visual update Reforged brings to all its beloved and behated characters is all the reason I needed to want to experience it again. It’s not perfect, and it’s not everything we may have been promised, but it’s still Warcraft 3. If I were judging it purely based on how good of a remaster it is, there’s not much to write home about and plenty of room for improvement. But taken as a whole, it’s still a great game nearly two decades after its initial release. And the relatively minor shortcomings of this edition shouldn’t stop you from returning to this classic age of Azeroth or diving in for the first time. - Len Hafer, February 5, 2020 Score: 7 Read the full Warcraft 3: Reforged review . Across three chapters, you focus mainly on Garek and Anya, completing quests across multiple areas of the Undercity and the surrounding countryside. There's quite a bit of progression to chew on, with the level cap extending all the way up to 20 by the end and a brand new system that allows you to equip tons of new gear in specific slots like in WoW or Diablo. Still, I longed for a little bit more variety. This is basically an RPG. There's really only one mission that makes use of RTS mechanics after the prologue. And since regular troops can only be bought at mercenary camps with the same money you could otherwise spend on gear, I found I was mostly just rolling with my two heroes. New units like the Forsaken Deathguard are too squishy to stick around for long, and feel like a waste of money when I could get a permanent upgrade like a new sword instead. Garek and Anya can also respawn for free at altars placed around the map (outside of a few scripted segments), which encouraged me to simply throw them at a challenge until it broke rather than try to return with backup. The writing isn't groundbreaking, but it does have that old school Blizzard touch. While I wouldn't say the writing in the campaign is groundbreaking, it does have that old school Blizzard touch. It's a little bit grittier and a little bit edgier than modern WoW. Getting to see the Undercity from a new angle and some major lore events like the rise of the Scarlet Crusade were neat. And Garek's journey to becoming the first Forsaken paladin had a worthwhile emotional payoff. Forsaken Kingdom also comes with a third, entirely new graphical style for Warcraft 3, the aforementioned "Definitive Edition" option. At first, I wasn't super impressed with this direction. It doesn't look great zoomed in during cutscenes, to be honest. A lot of the textures are extremely flat, matte, and almost unfinished-looking. You can see visible pixels on some of the armor where it transitions from the faction blue to the metallic edging. This is more apparent on some units than others, especially in the campaign. But when I loaded into a custom skirmish match against AI, I suddenly saw what Blizzard was going for. Playing zoomed out at a fast pace, I almost forgot I wasn't using the original 2003 graphics. It's like a magic trick. All the units and buildings look like how I remember them, just with higher fidelity. I suspect this will become the preferred way to play multiplayer and custom games for all but the most die-hard, low-polygon grognards. It's a bit unfortunate to me, then, that these visual goodies are so unevenly distributed. The Forsaken Kingdom campaign can only be played with the Definitive Edition graphics. (And, you know, that seems fair enough.) Multiplayer and skirmish let you pick between Classic, Reforged, or Definitive Edition. But if you want to revisit the still frankly superb Reign of Chaos and Frozen Throne campaigns – and you really should! – they only support Classic or Reforged, not Definitive. That's probably the most disappointing part of this whole package. It's unfortunate that the new visual goodies are so unevenly distributed. The other significant addition, and the one with a big impact on multiplayer, is Warcraft 3's first new tavern hero since the Alchemist and Firelord were added in 2004. This is the Forsaken Paladin, based on Garek, of course. He's in a bit of a strange thematic spot. After all, there's already the Human Paladin hero, and the Death Knight was originally designed as sort of a negative mirror image of that. So where does that leave the Forsaken Paladin? Well, he is an undea d neutral hero who can only heal the living, so he might be the least useful to Undead faction players, ironically. His Q ability is a dash that slows enemies it passes through, so he's quite mobile. As a strength hero, he is deadly in melee. His W is familiar to anyone who has played a WoW paladin with Consecration, which damages undead enemies and heals friendly living units in a small circle at his feet. He also has a passive aura that reduces magic damage taken and increases healing received. And his ult is an AoE purge/stun that heals nearby friendly units, with bonus healing and a short damage buff if the purge removed a debuff from them. This could definitely have some strong counterplay against certain builds, and I'm interested to see what pro players think of him. I like the way he brings a playstyle we've seen in spin-offs like Dota to the mix, though I think he might be a touch overpowered at the moment. I should also mention that the number of units in a control group has been doubled across all game modes. It's an ambitious change for a legacy game like this, and one I'm sure the old guard will groan about. But I think it's a positive one overall, from my spot down here in the tryhard seats.
items.title_en: Warcraft 3 Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom Review

items.title: Xbox Says Its Share of GTA 6 Preorders Matches Its Share of the Console Market, Following PS5 Dominance Claim
items.excerpt: Microsoft has stepped in to address a report that claimed GTA 6 preorders are “heavily skewed” toward PlayStation 5 over Xbox Series X and S.
items.content_text: Microsoft has stepped in to address a report that claimed GTA 6 preorders are “heavily skewed” toward PlayStation 5 over Xbox Series X and S. In a report about this week’s layoffs and studios reorganization at Xbox , The Verge’s Tom Warren said the PS5’s dominance over GTA 6 preorders was “ringing yet more alarm bells" about Xbox as a platform. However, Xbox CSO Matthew Ball insisted that Microsoft was “very happy” with GTA 6 preorders, and that its internal data showed preorders were matching “our share of the console market.” Here’s Ball’s statement in full: “Tom, we are very happy with GTA VI pre-orders. The title is breaking records for XBOX, we expect even more records will be broken throughout the fall, and our internal analysis shows our share of preorders to be matching our share of the console market.” While Sony does announce PS5 sales, Microsoft hasn’t announced a number for Xbox Series X and S sales in years. As of June 30, PS5 had sold more than 95 million units. Analysts have suggested the combined Xbox Series range is being outsold by the PS5 by at least a factor of 2:1. If that ratio holds true, there are likely twice as many GTA 6 preorders for PS5 than for Xbox Series X and S. Sony and Rockstar Games' partnership for GTA 6 wil be having a big impact on preorders, too. Sony has leaned heavily into GTA 6, which you can understand given we’re talking about a video game that is expected to break sales records and spark a surge in console sales. This has led to GTA 6 gameplay focusing on the PS5 version, the PS5 showing up in marketing materials for GTA 6, and even a custom GTA 6 UI for Sony’s console . Sony has published blog posts talking about the features of the PS5 that GTA 6 will use, such as the speaker in the DualSense controller and the pad's haptic feedback. Other additions to GTA 6's PS5 marketing campaign include a version of the PlayStation app logo on smartphones that features GTA 6 colors and pale tree fronds. So, with PlayStation’s partnership in full swing, preorders being “heavily skewed” toward PS5 shouldn’t come as much of a surprise to anyone. The Verge’s report also suggested that the Xbox “reset,” led by new CEO Asha Sharma, might be about making Xbox easier to spin off or operate as a wholly owned subsidiary, as has been suggested by prior reports elsewhere. GTA 6 launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S only on November 19.

items.title: New Saw Movie Taps Mike P. Nelson to Direct
items.excerpt: The next Saw movie has officially hired a director as it prepares for Jigsaw's next game.
items.content_text: The next Saw movie has officially hired a director as it prepares for Jigsaw's next game. Mike P. Nelson, an up-and-coming horror director responsible for films like the Wrong Turn reboot and Silent Night, Deadly Night, has been selected to direct the next Saw film. The flick is being penned by Gregory Weidman & Geoff Tock and produced by horror legends James Wan, Jason Blum, and Leigh Whannell. Wan and Whannell created the series as a disturbing short film before eventually expanding it into a gory low-budget feature. Wan largely moved on from Saw following the third film, going on to direct Insidious, The Conjuring, and blockbusters like Aquaman. He's expected to have a much more significant role in the next installment as Lionsgate attempts to bolster the franchise once again. Speaking on the decision to select Nelson as the director of the next chapter, Wan praised his style of filmmaking. did you miss me? pic.twitter.com/c6tpQwanFF — SAW (@Saw) September 24, 2026 “Making the original Saw was a defining experience for me, so it was essential to find a director who would honor that world," said Wan. "Mike has a raw, distinctive filmmaking voice with an inventive approach to the genre, and I believe he’ll bring something truly unique and special to the franchise.” Nelson was also excited about being able to take a crack at the beloved franchise. “Being asked to play in this twisted sandbox with James is nothing short of a dream come true," said Nelson. "Greg and Geoff and James have crafted such a wild script that brings the mystery of the original while exploring new insane bloody ideas that meld so well with the brutal moral compass of the franchise. Let the games begin!” It's unclear exactly what the next Saw film will entail. Saw X left the door open for more prequel movies, following Jigsaw's adventures prior to his death, but creative disagreements reportedly caused the film to stall out . The various creatives that worked on Saw X were expected to return for a sequel, but have since walked away from the franchise. As a result, it sounds like whatever comes next will be something very different. Wan and Whannell did confirm to Bloody Disgusting earlier this year that Jigsaw will play a significant role in the next Saw film, despite his death in the third movie. "Leigh and I, we’re not going to give too much away, but we don’t think you can make a Saw movie without Jigsaw. That’s the bottom line. items.title: How Silent Hill: Townfall Brings a New Perspective to the Iconic Horror Series
items.content_text: For nearly three decades, the Silent Hill series has evolved through new protagonists, settings, and approaches to psychological horror. Silent Hill: Townfall continues that tradition by introducing the franchise's first full-length first-person experience, a new setting outside the typical Silent Hill town, and a cast featuring acclaimed actors from film, television, and games. While previous entries have largely centered on the town of Silent Hill itself, Townfall takes you to St. Amelia, a remote Scottish island that’s been abandoned by its residents. Although the setting differs, the game continues to explore themes that have long defined the franchise. You play as Simon, a man with a connection to the island who begins the game armed with nothing more than a handheld CRTV, which serves as an evolution of concepts familiar to longtime fans. Similar to how earlier games used radio signals and environmental cues to build tension, Townfall's handheld device becomes a central tool for uncovering story details and navigating threats. These story details are tied to narrative-driven puzzles that will reveal past events or allow you to see how people lived in St. Amelia before it fell into its current state. They go a long way toward filling out the world and adding important details between major plot moments. When you use the CRTV to detect enemies, you’ll then have to choose how to deal with them. If you’re the type who likes to rush in and destroy as many enemies as you can, there are options for that. You’ll pick up melee weapons that you can use to block or swing in face-to-face combat, or you can use firearms for longer range damage while managing your limited ammo. For the more cautious among us, stealth is also a viable (and often preferable) option. The first-person perspective limits visibility and heightens the sense of danger, but that’s where the CRTV can help. It allows you to track movement even from behind cover, so you’re not forced to potentially reveal yourself just to figure out where enemies are. You can also use things in the environment to distract enemies and lure them away long enough for you to sneak past. The sense of tension is heightened by the sound design and music, with all the creaks, cries, and creepy noises you’d expect from the series. Townfall uses a dynamic soundtrack created by Canadian musician Pilotpriest that reacts to actions you and enemies make and shifts with the ebb and flow of combat and stealth. The voice cast is also a standout, including Emmy Award nominee Jovan Adepo, Emmy winner Terry O’Quinn, and Kezia Burrows from Observation, one of developer Screen Burn’s previous titles. Adepo plays Simon, while O’Quinn plays Richard, a voice beckoning Simon back to the island. Burrows plays Zoe, a former resident of St. Amelia whose voice reaches out to Simon through his CRTV. The cast brings to life a story that’s haunting for more reasons than just the creepy monsters plaguing the island. It deals with introspection, loss, and the consequences of past decisions, with the island and its current nature shaped by that past. Silent Hill: Townfall brings several notable firsts for the franchise, but it still focuses on the psychological horror that has defined Silent Hill for nearly 30 years. That combination of new and familiar makes it approachable for series newcomers as well as veterans. It’s out now on PlayStation 5 and PC.

items.title: Robert Pattinson Casts Doubt on a Crossover Between His Batman and James Gunn's Superman
items.excerpt: Robert Pattinson has trouble imagining a universe where his Batman and James Gunn's Superman could co-exist, casting doubt on a potential crossover.
items.content_text: Robert Pattinson has trouble imagining a universe where his Batman and James Gunn's Superman could co-exist, casting doubt on a potential crossover. Speaking with LADbible , Pattinson stated that he thinks it would be difficult to pluck his take on a dark, grounded Batman and drop him in James Gunn's lighter, more fantastical DC universe. “I think it would be kind of tough to have this version of Bruce outside of that world," he said. "It's one of the only characters, I guess because of the length of the shoots, but also it's such a specific kind of [style], the tone of it gets inside you. I remember that happened to me the last time I did it, it took a while. You’re just in the dark, the whole time. Both mood-wise and light-wise, I can't see anything for like months. It does affect you, like you feel strange afterwards." Fans have been somewhat split for a while now over whether Pattinson should also play Batman in Gunn's main DC universe, or if he should remain relegated to his own separate part of the multiverse, and it seems like Pattinson believes the latter makes the most sense. James Gunn himself has said that they're developing a Batman film that will follow an older Bruce Wayne, with Damian Wayne as his sidekick. There have been very few updates about that film, with some believing DC may wait for Matt Reeves to conclude his story before introducing another Batman in order to avoid confusing audiences. Of course, plans could change at any minute, and they could choose to leverage Pattinson's Batman in the DCU. Despite the major difference in tone between The Batman and Gunn's Superman, the current DCU does have some darker stories on offer. Lanterns is proof that a grounded and more mature story can still easily fit into the larger DCU. Next month, we'll also get Clayface , which is set to be an R-rated body horror film set in the same universe as Superman, Lanterns, and Supergirl. There's room for a bit of everything, and some think that the strong contrast between Pattinson's Batman and David Corenswet's Superman could provide for a charming take on World's Finest. Maybe one day it will all happen, but if Pattinson's comments are anything to go by, it won't be anytime soon. The Batman Part 2 hits theaters on February 18, 2027. Man of Tomorrow , the sequel to Superman, will fly into theaters on July 9, 2027.

items.title: Spider-Man's Jacob Batalon Explains What Destin Daniel Cretton Likes Most About Naruto and Why Team 7 Could Be the Movie's Focus
items.excerpt: Jacob Batalon shed some light on what Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton likes most about Naruto, giving fans a tentative idea of the direction his live-action adaptation of the iconic anime series might take.
items.content_text: Jacob Batalon shed some light on what Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton likes most about Naruto, giving fans a tentative idea of the direction his live-action adaptation of the iconic anime series might take. Jacob Batalon, who plays Peter Parker’s bestie Ned Leeds in the Tom Holland films, sat down for an episode of The Anime Effect podcast with Crunchyroll on September 19 to chat about all things anime. Naturally, the topic of Destin Daniel Cretton’s live-action Naruto movie came up, prompting the hosts to quiz him about what the Brand New Day director likes best about the classic anime. Speaking from his own perspective, Batalon said that he feels like Cretton is drawn to the origin story of Team 7 — the main group of characters in the original Naruto series, initially made up of Naruto, Sasuke, Sakura, and its leader, Kakashi. “I think he likes the aspect of Team 7 and their coming-up story,” he explained. “I think that’s really cool. I think for a lot of storytelling in movies, when you’re trying to move from a specific IP to movies meant for everyone, you have to start somewhere where everyone kind of understands where they’re coming from. I think a lot of origin story-type things are really important when you’re trying to tell a story that not everyone is accustomed to. “I think that could be a main thing. But also, he’s been doing this for a long time. I have no idea what he’s doing now. He could’ve completely changed it all and probably made Orochimaru the main character. I don’t know. He could've done something crazy,” he laughed. While Batalon made it clear that he isn’t certain how Cretton’s movie will actually pan out, it wouldn’t be surprising if we saw him adapt Team 7’s come-up journey; centering on the main group of characters and following their storyline would make sense, especially since certain actors are already reportedly in talks to take on the roles of some of Team 7’s members. For instance, Charles Melton was reported to be in final negotiations to play Kakashi in August, choosing to move away from X-Men’s Beast in Marvel Studios’ upcoming reboot film. The search for Naruto is still underway, though. An open casting call was put out this summer, reportedly looking for young male actors between 16 and 20 years old who are “athletic, energetic, expressive” and speak fluent English. Masashi Kishimoto, the mangaka who created Naruto, has stated that he is extremely excited about the movie, writing a statement on the series’ official website saying he “cannot believe” his manga is being adapted into a major Hollywood film. “Right now, miracles are happening to me, one after another. My work, Naruto, is truly, truly becoming a Hollywood movie! And an even greater miracle is that the film will be directed by the one and only Destin Daniel Cretton. I still cannot believe it!” he said. Image Credits: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images / Masashi Kishimoto / Shueisha

items.title: Bungie Finally Details Radical Changes for Marathon
items.excerpt: It's no secret that Marathon has had a rough time since launching in March 2026, but Bungie is hard at work on new game modes that it's hoping will breathe new life into the game.
items.content_text: It's no secret that Marathon has had a rough time since launching in March 2026, but Bungie is hard at work on new game modes that it's hoping will breathe new life into the game. Prevously, Bungie teased that new game modes were coming to Marathon, and even released an 'experimental' mode with Vault Breaker. Today, the company posted on Twitter detailing the new ways people can play game. The Extraction modes that it was launched with aren't going anywhere, but Bungie will be adding a team deathmatch mode, along with new PvE modes that should be reminiscent of Destiny. Bungie will also be expanding Perimeter, essentially its tutorial level, to be closer in scope to other full zones. Bungie's goal seems to be limiting the friction that new players feel and letting them filter themselves into more familiar gameplay types. That should, in theory, let people ease themselves into the traditional extraction mode that's proven so divisive. https://t.co/SKfaCog1Aw — Marathon (@MarathonTheGame) September 24, 2026 All of this new content and game modes aren't going to come at the same time, though. In its post, Bungie laid out a road map, with a Nightfall refresh coming first in October. Then, in December, there will be the Symbiosis update, which will bring Marathon's first permanent PvE mode, along with Team Deathmatch. Bungie doesn't go into a lot of detail on what this new PvE mode will look like, but says it will give more details closer to launch. In March, which will mark Marathon's one-year anniversary, Bungie is planning a much larger update that will apparently link all of these gameplay modes together. There will also be a new onboarding experience, which the company previewed a little bit in a behind-the-scenes documentary that dropped earlier today. There will even be a giant Tick Queen. All of these updates seem like a promising way to bring players back to Marathon, but only time will tell if it's enough. Either way, Bungie will be returning to Destiny, starting with returning vaulted content back to Destiny 2. Beyond that, it seems like fans have convinced Bungie to return to Destiny long-term , with developer Poria Torkan saying, "Bungie wouldn't be what it is today without it. It's the foundation upon which everything else rests, and we are absolutely not done with Destiny."

items.title: Counter-Strike Co-Creator Says Gabe Newell Got So Obsessed With Mongolian Throat Singing at Valve HQ That Staff Started Closing Their Office Doors to Escape the Noise
items.excerpt: In an interview with game consultant Indie Game Joe, Counter-Strike co-creator Minh Le revealed a hilarious anecdote about Valve boss Gabe Newell that’s going viral for just how absurd it is.
items.content_text: In an interview with game consultant Indie Game Joe, Counter-Strike co-creator Minh Le revealed a hilarious anecdote about Valve boss Gabe Newell that’s going viral for just how absurd it is. Le claimed that, at one point during his tenure, Newell became so enamored with the concept of Mongolian throat singing that he couldn’t stop practicing it in Valve’s corporate offices — to the point where his employees started closing their office doors to avoid the noise. If you’re not familiar with Mongolian throat singing, it’s a vocal technique most popularly associated with the people of Tuvan, a region in Russia located northwest of Mongolia. The Tuvan people call it Khöömei , and it’s achieved by using circular breathing to produce two or more notes simultaneously. It’s a seriously impressive talent that has become popularized over time, and has been utilized in a number of famous films and TV series (like the Sardaukar chant in the first Dune movie , for example). Apparently, Newell wanted to try it out for himself — but his choice to practice in the workplace wasn’t necessarily conducive to a collaborative work environment. “At one point, he got into Mongolian throat singing,” Le explained . “In Mongolia, they have these throat singers that sing really interestingly, just using their throats. Gabe watched this documentary on them. He got really fascinated with this concept, and he started to practice that. He was doing it throughout the office. He would just walk around the halls doing this throat-singing thing. “You would hear him try to sing with his throat as he’s walking down the hall. I remember a lot of the people in the office were kind of annoyed with this, because, you know, it's kind of loud, right? …He would do it daily. People would just start closing their doors. It started to become quite a closed office. It was an interesting time. Thankfully, he didn’t do it for more than — I think it lasted for about five months.” As pointed out by a commenter on Instagram , Le isn’t the only Valve veteran to have mentioned Gabe’s Mongolian throat singing phase; in the Half-Life 2: 20th Anniversary Documentary , senior developer Charlie Brown mentioned that the office was “normally pretty vibrant and loud,” with staff “riding scooters in the hallway and doing all sorts of stuff,” while Gabe was “Tuvan throat singing.” Fans can watch the man practicing for themselves in the Dota 2 Mega-Kills Announcement Pack video on YouTube , which shows him warming up a sound booth as part of a skit. Unsurprisingly, Le’s most recent story has resulted in no end of jokes and memes about Gabe’s Mongolian throat singing phase, with fans joking that he “yearns for the steppe” and affectionately dubbing him “Gabe-is Khan.” This is the latest amusing news to come from Newell after he purchased a $70.8 million super mansion in June, which came with its own underground tunnel. You know, in case the Headcrabs try to get him or something. Image Credits: YouTube - Valve
